title: system design requirements estimation capacity and tradeoffs
concepts: System design starts by defining the outcome, actors, functional behavior, constraints, workload shape, and the qualities the system must demonstrate; architecture cannot optimize an unstated requirement.

Quality targets should be observable and testable. A vague request such as 'fast' or 'highly available' needs a workload, measurement point, threshold, time window, and acceptable failure or cost level.
Capacity estimates are models, not promises: estimate average and peak load, per-request resource use, growth, redundancy, and headroom, then test the model against measured workload behavior.
Architecture decisions balance reliability, security, cost, operational effort, and performance efficiency; improving one quality can consume resources or reduce another.
Plan for overload and failure as well as normal operation. Define graceful degradation, capacity limits, recovery targets, and the evidence that would trigger a design revision.
Record assumptions and uncertainty explicitly. Prefer a reversible, testable decision when the evidence is weak, and revisit the decision when workload or business conditions change.
